steps.content: August, N.F. 115. The destruction of BR-005 turned the tide of war.

The Farland Alliance was forced into a full retreat. For DisCity, it was more than a victory; it was the moment they seized decisive strategic superiority.

At the center of it all was General Augustus. Her legendary military success granted her unprecedented influence.

Now, the city holds its breath. Will Paradeisos appoint her to a higher office? Will she seek new battlefields?

The rumors are a constant hum, yet the profound reverence for her—or more accurately, for pure, unassailable strength—never wavers.

You, too, once felt that reverence.

Having stood with her, breached the Black Ring, and rescued Hella, you placed her on a pedestal.
But perspectives shift. And in the space of a few short days, yours began to change...

September 1, N.F. 115
Bureau Office
After BR-005, the MBCC mailroom has been nearly buried. Not in debris, but in gifts from General Augustus.

They have been pouring in daily—gourmet food, vintage wine, and tailored suits, punctuated by endless invitations to galas and yacht parties. But the most absurd by far is one piece from her personal collection: a hulking metal horse statue.

Reportedly salvaged from the BR-005 battlefield, she found the metal horse "very cool" but had no space for it in a Nirvana Port undergoing reconstruction. In a stroke of what she called generosity, General Augustus decided to let you display it for a few days.
You try to follow her reasoning.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: So, do you like my gift? Any fun plans for the weekend?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: How does a General have this much free time? Some of us are chained to our desks. You get to relax; I get to burn the midnight oil.
Hearty laughter echoes on the other end of the terminal.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Hahaha! After all we've been through, you still don't see it? Life can end in an instant. That's not a reason to hide in your office; it's a reason to live.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Especially for a workaholic like you... you might just drop dead from exhaustion one day, who knows?
You maintain your composure; a few provocative words from her are no match for your current equanimity. Adjusting your mindset, you respond with measured dignity.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Thanks to the endurance training from your unit, I'm good for a few more all-nighters. Now, if you'll excuse me, duty calls.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Hmm... brushing me off like that... Could it be...
Her contemplative tone gives you pause. Overtime is a convenient excuse, but you know the truth is more complicated. You are, after all, facing the most formidable woman in DisCity.

Is it politics? A conflict of interest? Or are you simply wary of being swept up by her overwhelming charisma? With your comrade-in-arms chapter closing, you haven't yet found the new script for your relationship. You wonder if she has, either.
Regardless, she speaks up.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Could it be you're sulking because <color=#fb9259>I</color> was the one who pulled little Hella out of the Black Ring, stealing <color=#fb9259>your</color> heroic moment?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Don't take it to heart. After all, in this world, the strong call the shots—
Jump
CLANK! You ended the call and blocked her number in one furious motion. Your terminal smashes against the wall, a victim of your fury.
The damage she inflicts isn't physical; it's a slow burn of pure frustration. You'll die from rage long before overwork claims you. Did you ever truly respect her? Really??
As the thought echoes in your mind, an elegant hand appears in the doorway, calmly retrieving the device you just condemned.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: Even the most durable device has its limits, Chief. And with reconstruction costs being what they are, our budget for replacements isn't quite what it used to be.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: I'd advise taking good care of this one. It's about to become extremely useful.

Seeing an old friend should be a rare pleasure, and a part of you is genuinely glad—his survival is a relief. The expected thing would be to exchange pleasantries, to fall into that easy rhythm. But you can't.
The crisis is far from over, and the 9th Agency is at the very epicenter of it all. An intelligence agent shouldn't have time for casual visits. Which means this is anything but casual.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's good to see you in one piece. But... you don't just drop by for a chat at a time like this. What's wrong?

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: You always did cut straight to the heart of the matter. You're correct. A concerning situation is developing within the city-state. The 9th Agency is preoccupied with external threats, leaving us stretched too thin to address it properly.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: So, I've come to seek your counsel. And, if I may be so bold, to ask you to leverage your... unique rapport with <color=#fb9259>a certain individual</color>.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: Naturally, I'm referring to the most prominent, politically sensitive, and frankly, sleep-depriving figure right now: <color=#fb9259>General Augustus</color>.
He hands you back the terminal you just threw. A single prompt glows on the screen: a data transfer request.

After the Ash campaign, DisCity's "savior," General Augustus, never bothered to leave. Instead of leading her Shattered Blade unit back to Nirvana Port, she has embedded herself in the city's elite social circuit. Or, more accurately, the elite now curate their events specifically for her.

<size=40>Activity Log 1:</size>
<color=#fb9259>N.F. 115/8/29</color> Attended a celebration banquet hosted by Public Security Bureau Chief Ford, a man previously suspected of involvement in the Euphoria case.

<size=40>Activity Log 2:</size>
<color=#fb9259>N.F. 115/8/30</color> Attended a covert meeting at the Jacknal Estate. The purpose is unknown. The owner, Penn Jacknal, is a suspect in Hypercube smuggling operations.

<size=40>Activity Log 3:</size>
<color=#fb9259>N.F. 115/8/31</color> Made a high-profile appearance at a joint reception hosted by the Harrington and Frank families, where she reportedly made shocking statements about conventional trade with the Outlands.
The report further notes a trail of suspicious financial transactions and regulatory violations, as multiple institutions have bent their own rules to accommodate her.
To the public, Augustus is a war hero basking in well-earned glory. But beneath the surface, her presence is a destabilizing force, sending shockwaves through the city's power structures.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: As you know, the General promised to return to Nirvana Port to regroup and await further orders. The agreed-upon deadline, however, has come and gone, with no sign of her departure.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: Her troops are still here. And what's more, she's using her victory as political capital, maneuvering through every sector of the city, expanding her influence. Her intentions... are unclear.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Augustus is bold, I'll give her that. Maybe even flashy. But she's always been straightforward with me. Is that really how the 9th Agency sees her? Or is this the view from... higher up?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Are you telling me she's being labeled a threat? That you think she's making a power grab?

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: ...Chief, you must understand. Compared to the long history she has written, your time with her has been but a brief chapter.
You read on, confusion giving way to disbelief, then to stunned silence. The revelation on the screen is impossible. Your eyes lock on the words, refusing to process them.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...What is this?!

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: Every detail there is a verifiable fact, a matter of historical record. We've fabricated nothing. DisCorps were vital allies in our recent fight; that is true. But it seems the General has not entirely left her... shadowed past behind. She is playing a deeper game.
His focus remains locked on the intelligence in your hands. A solemn undercurrent now runs through his tone.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: The General holds a unique interest in you. We need you to use that. Learn what she is truly planning. If our concerns are misplaced, then we will all rest easier. But if they are not...

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: ...Then DisCity may face a threat far more dangerous than anything the Outlands could muster.
After a moment of hesitation, you set aside the other reports in your hands and accept the mission.
[Scene Change: Interrogation Room]

The next day, against all reason, she comes. Catherine Augustus Andohar—the general who repelled the great enemy, the leader of the Shattered Blade, DisCity's most celebrated figure—has accepted your discourteous "invitation." She forsakes a dozen high-society galas to descend into your austere, oppressive interrogation room.
That chair has held countless notorious Sinners. Yet none occupy it as she does. She sits with an air of poised imperiousness, not as a guest in your domain, but as its sovereign.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: So this is where you finally decide to ask me, after playing hard to get for so long? Charming.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Off the battlefield, your sense of decorum is... remarkably flexible.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Thank you for accepting MBCC's invitation, General Augustus.
Hearing you address her this way, she raises an eyebrow.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This isn't a formal interrogation. Just a routine inquiry. Since you've been at WhiteSands for years, you're likely unaware of the recent policy changes in DisCity.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Being a Sinner is no longer a crime. Pass our psychological and ability assessments, get an MBCC safety certification, and you can move freely in public. You'll have the full rights of any DisCitizen.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Hmm... Acceptable. Not much different from how things are now.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Well then, let's see what the Chief of Minos can do with a suspect like me. The rumors flying about you are... fascinating.
A mere two hours ago, you could have dismissed her methods as unprofessional. Now, that luxury is gone.

options: Ask why she's staying in the city

choices.text: Ask why she's staying in the city

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Isn't this the great DisCity? All my family's mansions and estates are here. Am I not allowed to come home? Or is a general not permitted to take a vacation?

options: You call bringing an entire stationed military unit a "vacation"?

choices.text: You call bringing an entire stationed military unit a "vacation"?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: My troops have weathered storms for years and just won a war. They deserve to enjoy the peace. Is there a problem with a commander looking after her own?

options: But the places you've been visiting are suspicious.

steps.content: test
test
test
test
test
test
test
It's the same classified document from the 9th Agency, cataloging all her contacts with numerous high-ranking officials.
Subsequent verification has linked a significant number of these individuals to active investigations for wartime betrayal and systemic corruption.
She listens, her eyes locked on yours. As you speak, her gaze sharpens from casual attention to a blade's point of focus.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Is there a problem with my social calendar? Does our austere Chief find my taste in associates too... lavish?

options: It's who you're meeting with that concerns me.
It's why you're meeting with them that concerns me.

choices.text: It's who you're meeting with that concerns me.
It's why you're meeting with them that concerns me.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I have friends who've briefed me on these people. I know their backgrounds. By associating with them, you're only tarnishing your own reputation.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Oh? And was that... your friend the Speaker who told you that? Or perhaps the friend who happens to be the former Speaker's... illegitimate daughter?
Her gaze is a physical pressure, and her tone, sharp enough to cut, sends a jolt of ice down your spine.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Who my sources are isn't the point. What are you playing at, Augustus?
Augustus gives a soft chuckle.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: What do you think? You've investigated me so thoroughly. Or perhaps... your real interest isn't in me at all, but in the <color=#fb9259>DisCorps</color> standing behind me?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Go on, then. Tell me what you've uncovered.
A new edge enters her voice. Your body reacts as if to a physical threat—muscles coiling, your grip on the files turning into a defensive clutch.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...After DisCity's independence, your faction rode the momentum of the Independence War to an overwhelming election victory. Within two years, you'd pacified the satellite towns, bringing security and prosperity to the entire periphery.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But soon after, the DisCorps under <color=#fb9259>Dravyn's</color> command twisted. He waged brutal campaigns abroad while enforcing an iron grip at home... He led this city into a long, dark era.
A cold sweat pricks at your hairline as you lay out the information. Augustus doesn't interrupt; she merely observes, her eyes alight with undisguised amusement.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: And what does that history lesson have to do with me? Didn't your files mention I was asleep for most of it?
Indeed, for DisCity in the fight for independence, a Sinner who could control magnetic fields was a priceless strategic asset, one capable of tipping the vast military scales against the metropoles.
To preserve this power and stave off Mania corruption, Catherine Augustus Andohar was placed in cryosleep shortly after independence, following the liberation of several key satellite towns.
By the time she awoke, it was already N.F. 103, long after DisCorps had been reorganized into the FAC. But... is she truly as disconnected from it all as she seems?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The records are clear. He gave you medals and promotions outside the chain of command. He personally led you into battle, and rumors suggest he was grooming you as his successor.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: To treat your war-induced Mania intensification, he personally ordered EDGE to develop cryosleep technology, all to ensure you would survive until a cure could be found.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That man is regarded as the greatest dictator in DisCity's history, a figure who's still controversial today. And you... you were like a daughter to him.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Are you saying you knew nothing about what he was doing? That you have no responsibility for it?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: "Like a daughter"... Hah! If that old grouch heard you say that, he'd be spinning in his grave!
She dismisses the most insignificant point of your accusation with a light laugh, yet her voice retains a strange, almost fond warmth.
Mid-laughter, her eyes find yours. The warmth vanishes, replaced by a focus so intense it feels like a physical pressure.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Go on. I'm listening.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Marshal Dravyn's prestige from the Independence War gave him immense power. But that power corrupted him. It concentrated in his hands until he became a tyrant.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: By the end of his first term, slow reconstruction was turning people against him. Facing electoral defeat, he refused to step down. He rigged the vote and forced his way back into office, becoming the longest-ruling dictator in DisCity's history.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: His solution to internal strife was external war. He plundered abroad and crushed dissent at home. Corruption was rampant. The city-state kept rotting... until the DisSea Explosion in N.F. 84 finally forced his hand.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Continue.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...After the explosion, the Black Ring returned. Mania catastrophes were everywhere. Dravyn had no choice but to cooperate with EDGE. He ceded authority, merged the military into the FAC, a united front against the Mania.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: He "stepped down" as Speaker to become the FAC's first Commander-in-Chief. The title changed, but his grip on power didn't. Not until the Eclipse Operation failed in N.F. 103. After that disaster, with public outrage and the FAC broken... the Marshal finally fell. He died in bitterness and obscurity.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: —That's the official record. The rumor is he couldn't live with his failure. That he took his own life.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And you woke up in N.F. 103. After Dravyn's death, when EDGE appointed Adrian Sterling as the new Commander-in-Chief, you refused his orders. You took a faction of DisCorps and left the city.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: It's been a long time since anyone has recounted this story to me. Go on.
The words die in your throat. A different kind of cold, one of pure dread, seizes you, locking your jaw and making speech impossible.

options: What are you trying to accomplish by coming back now?

choices.text: What are you trying to accomplish by coming back now?

steps.content: She holds your gaze, relentless and silent, until the question evaporates from your mind and all that remains is the slow, suffocating weight of her attention.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Are you afraid of me?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Heh, you should be, boy. Do you really think I can't do anything just because we're on your turf?
steps.female_content: Heh, you should be, girl. Do you really think I can't do anything just because we're on your turf?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Perceptive. That's more like it. You should be, boy. Do you really think I can't do anything just because we're on your turf?
steps.female_content: Perceptive. That's more like it. You should be, girl. Do you really think I can't do anything just because we're on your turf?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Your pathetic security system can't even detect a killing intent this clear.

Bzzt— Blackness ensues as the Mania field kills the lights. The Sinner's restraints disengage immediately. In the heartbeat that follows, cold metal shrieks as it clamps around your wrists and ankles, chaining you to the chair.
Your struggles are useless. Across from you, the architect of this chaos lounges in her seat, a motionless silhouette in the dark—a sated predator observing its captive prey.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Curious? Let me give you a demonstration of how we used to handle interrogations back in the tyrannical DisCorps era.

An unseen force lifts your chair, and you with it. You glide helplessly through the oppressive dark, drawn directly toward her. Augustus remains seated, merely planting a foot against your chair to halt your approach with nonchalance.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: I've completed my registration. I haven't misused my powers. By the book, you have no grounds to interrogate me. Besides, you've been "too busy" to see me.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: So why the sudden change of heart?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Still holding back? Look around. The surveillance is offline; this is our private little space now. I can do anything I want to you, and we have all the time in the world for a... heart-to-heart.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Your recent behavior has raised concerns. After our victory, a lot of dubious elements have resurfaced. Instead of keeping your distance, you're meeting with them. People are naturally questioning your intentions.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Oh? And what does that have to do with you?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Didn't you solemnly declare you'd "only fight Mania and only go to Mania battlefields"? It's only been a few days, and now you're dabbling in political scandals again?
Her questioning leaves you speechless.
Indeed, you have no official reason to be involved. She truly hasn't misused her abilities, you no longer report to the 9th Agency, and the MBCC has no stake. So... why are you risking her wrath?
Doubt flashes through your mind, but now is not the time to waver. Augustus demands an answer.

options: Tell her about your mission first

choices.text: Tell her about your mission first

steps.content: You press your lips together, offering only silence. To your surprise, a spark of genuine amusement lights her eyes.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Not talking, hmm... Let me guess. Did someone put you up to this? "Expressed their concerns"?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Some reliable people are concerned about your intentions. They asked me to look into it.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: They told you quite a bit, didn't they? To be careful around me? To stay away? Or perhaps... to deliver a warning?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Who</color> told you to probe me like this?
Her voice drops to a glacial temperature. An unseen magnetic force wrenches your chair forward, slamming you into the direct, cutting line of her stare.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: How did the person who gave you this "mission" describe me? Rebel, usurper, thug, heir to a dictator, returning aspirant... what else?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Then, did they tell you this...
The cold leather of her glove closes around your jaw. With irresistible force, she yanks you forward, pulling your ear to within a breath of her mouth.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: The second Commander of the Independence Army, the first democratically elected Speaker, the first FAC Commander-in-Chief—<color=#fb9259>Marshal Dravyn Steel</color> did not commit suicide.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: He was killed by his <color=#fb9259>most trusted subordinate</color>... These ambitious jackals waited until the old Marshal was in his twilight years, then made their move to seize his fading power. They delivered the final blow to the already weakened FAC, ensuring it would become nothing more than EDGE's puppet.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: They left that part out, did they? Good. Then you should hear it from me. And we can discuss... other things, too.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Like what we really did. To our own people, to others... Not just numbers in a report. The real stories. The kind they'd never dare mention now, during DisCity's glorious triumph. It's far too shameful.
[Jasmine Flashback]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: <color=#dg1f1f><size=44><i>Don't touch me!</color></size><i>

You deploy the prohibition. It's the first time you've used that command on her. For a single, heart-stopping moment, you see it: a flash of pure, unadulterated murderous intent in her eyes, there and gone, but utterly real.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: So that's how you use those shackles... Heh. No wonder so many were desperate to bring you back.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Mmph—!
The crimson spikes lance through her frame, forcing her to release you. But the hovering shards of metal ignore the command, darting forward to clamp over your mouth, silencing you utterly.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Go on, then. Let's see what else you can do...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If you want to talk, then tell me this: Why do treasonous, irredeemable remnants of the DisCorps have such close ties with the current Commander-in-Chief?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Back in N.F. 103, when the FAC was at its weakest, why didn't your "arrogant and disloyal" faction—you included—seize power? And who had the strength to exile you all?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And... what were you really angry about just now? This "mission"... What are you using me to fight against?
No answer comes, but the pressure pinning you down slackens by a fraction. Augustus opens her mouth to speak when suddenly—

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief!
The door bursts open as Nightingale interrupts the conversation.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: General Augustus, this is a serious misunderstanding. Please, allow me to explain.
Her grip doesn't yield. Instead, she settles back against the chair, tilting her head in a cool, appraising stare directed at your adjutant.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: I must say, I never imagined DisCity would treat a victorious general like this. What's the saying? "Kill the goose that lays the golden eggs"? Though, your Chief here has no way to restrain me.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: You have my sincere apologies. The 9th Agency inadvertently implicated you during their investigation into the Sillage Society. There have been individuals with ulterior motives attempting to approach you since your victory. Our intention was only to advise caution.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: However, a person of significant authority has vouched for you. All official suspicions have been cleared. We only need to complete some paperwork to formally restore your freedom.
Augustus holds her in a cold, silent stare for a protracted moment before the force field restraining you finally dissolves.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: So it's that little spider... Too busy to keep tabs on me personally this time? Heh...
She scans the documents, and you both see it: the cited author's name—
<color=#fb9259>Barry Orwell</color>—the Council's recording clerk who publicly challenged her at various wartime gatherings.
A slow, knowing smirk spreads across her lips. But your mind is already elsewhere, grappling with a far more critical implication.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What do you mean, "cleared"? My interrogation isn't finished. This is far from over.
Nightingale's face loses all color, her words catching in her throat. Before a single syllable can form, Augustus's voice slices through the tension.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: It means someone in higher places wants to stand behind me and ride the wave of my success. Well, I suppose I should humor them...

She frees you from the chair's magnetic grip. The clatter of fallen metal pieces is the sound of the interrogation being forcibly concluded. Then, as if flipping a switch, she is all soft smiles and soothing gestures, gently straightening your clothes.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: My apologies for misunderstanding you. It's been a complicated time. I may have been on edge. I hope I didn't frighten you.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Perfect timing. I have a banquet to attend. You should join me. Consider it my way of making amends. I'll even let you get a good whiff of the sweet scent of power.
She moves to leave, but as she passes you, she leans in close enough for her shadow to fall across your vision, dominating your field of view.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: After all, weren't you ordered to keep a close eye on me?
